applyTo: "docs/**/*.md"

# Reviewing this project's plans, ADRs and notes

For repo-wide conventions, see [`copilot-instructions.md`](../copilot-instructions.md) and `AGENTS.md` at the repository root.

These files are a decision record, not specification prose. Most of what looks like a defect in them is a deliberate convention.

- **`docs/notes/` is the exception to most of what follows, and reading it under the rules for a plan gets the review backwards.** A note records how some part of this project currently behaves, not what was decided or what was done, and it is a **living document**: it is corrected in place, its figures are claims about the repository as it stands, and its `path:line` citations resolve against `HEAD`. A stale measurement in a note **is** a defect and is worth flagging, where the same staleness in `docs/plans/done/` is the format working correctly.
- **Done plans are historical records.** Files in `docs/plans/done/` are completed plan documents preserved for reference. They may not match the final implementation. Do not flag discrepancies between done plan content and the actual codebase, and do not suggest prose or wording edits to them. **This covers `path:line` citations, snippets and identifier names**, which record what was true or proposed when the plan was written. A plan added to `done/` by the same pull request that implements it is still a historical record: check its citations against the branch's merge-base, not against the head. A `path:line` citation in a **todo** plan or an ADR is a claim about current code and may be checked.
- **The build plan at `docs/plans/2026-09-13-savera-build-plan.md` is permanent.** It is the master plan, never moves to `done/`, and gains a `### Phase N outcomes (complete)` subsection per phase. Its Findings and Environment status tables are dated measurements from 2026-09-13 and stay as measured; later facts land in the outcomes subsections and in the Status lines of its Risks entries. Do not suggest updating a dated table to match a later outcome.
- **Plans and ADRs state measured facts at a point in time, and that is the format working correctly.** "Measured on 2026-09-14", "no host implements it", "the working assumption for budgets is 4" are records of what was true when written, carrying their own dates so a later reader can decide whether to re-measure. **Do not suggest making them conditional, hedged, or future-proof.**
- **An anchored figure and a present-tense figure are allowed to differ.** "fosforo measured 24 seconds over 29 runs" describes another repository's history; a note's table states what is true here now. When they disagree, the repair is a fresh measurement of the present-tense figure, never editing the anchored one.
- **ADRs are superseded, not edited.** A decision that has changed, or a value a later phase measured, gets an amendment section at the foot of the file; the original text stays standing even where the amendment refines it. Do not suggest reconciling the two, and do not flag the contradiction as an inconsistency. Several ADRs deliberately leave a value open, such as the solver's iteration count or the internal sample rate, naming the phase that measures it; that is not a missing value.
- **Refusals are recorded on purpose.** Sections and ADRs that say what the project will not do, and why, are load-bearing: sample playback, waveguides, the European harmonium, in-rank reed coupling and a WebView UI are recorded refusals or deferrals, not gaps. Do not suggest implementing them; suggest a superseding ADR if there is a genuine new reason.
- **`docs/design/peti-physical-model-brainstorm.md` is preserved verbatim and is not maintained prose.** It is the map of territory the build plan grew from, and several of its claims are corrected by the build plan's findings rather than by editing it: its 8x oversampling figure, its subcritical jump at onset, its Q of 95, its 4 to 6 reed polyphony, its in-rank reed coupling, and its arXiv citation of the Millot and Baumann paper. Do not flag any of those, its bare URLs, its code fence without a language, or its formatting, and do not ask for it to be reconciled with the build plan. Prettier and markdownlint both exclude it for this reason.
- **When a diff corrects a measured figure, check whether the old value survives elsewhere, and say where.** Figures are quoted across `AGENTS.md`, the ADRs, the build plan, the notes and config comments. Grep the old value and report every live occurrence. Occurrences in `docs/plans/done/` are not live.
- **Prose is one long line per paragraph.** `MD013` is disabled in `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`. Do not suggest hard-wrapping at any column.
- **Prettier owns every table's shape, and `MD060` verifies it.** Do not suggest a delimiter row's form or a cell's padding as a defect; `npm run format` settles it.
